event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: MGM’s 2022-02-25 Form 10-K portrays COVID-19 as an immediate, multi-faceted threat that has already eroded revenues and liquidity and could intensify in unknown ways.  Management describes concrete, realized damage—property closures, reduced travel demand, supply-chain breakdowns and labour shortages—while also warning that emerging variants or renewed governmental restrictions could again shutter properties or suppress consumer activity.  The language is highly specific (e.g., references to Omicron, Macau travel curbs, labour and materials shortages) and repeatedly uses materiality qualifiers, showing the risk is both present and quantitatively significant.  Because the filing date is less than three years after the pandemic’s onset, Time Decay permits upper-range scoring.  No strong mitigating controls are offered beyond generic statements that restrictions have “eased,” so overall risk evidence remains elevated.

evidence_list.snippet: The global COVID-19 pandemic has continued to materially impact our business, financial results and liquidity, and such impact could worsen and last for an unknown period of time.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemic to ongoing material impact on business, financials and liquidity.
Uses strong qualifier “materially impact,” signalling severity.
Highlights possibility of worsening and indefinite duration, increasing forward-looking risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, quantified-in-words statement of current and potentially worsening material harm merits a very high score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, due to the COVID-19 pandemic, our business has also been impacted by labor shortages and global supply chain disruptions.

components.reason: Connects pandemic directly to labour shortages (operational risk).
Connects pandemic directly to supply-chain disruptions (another operational risk).
States impact already occurring (“has also been impacted”).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies two concrete, present-tense operational disruptions tied to COVID-19, justifying a high risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, the spread of new variants, including omicron, has had a material impact on domestic and international travel, which has resulted in reduced demand for hotel rooms, convention space and other casino resorts amenities.

components.reason: Cites variants (Omicron) as causal factor, showing evolving threat.
Links to reduced customer demand across core revenue streams (rooms, conventions, amenities).
Uses phrase “material impact,” stressing severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Details concrete revenue-line erosion from variants, yielding a strong though slightly lower score than direct financial metric references.

evidence_list.snippet: While restrictions have eased throughout 2021, new restrictions to combat the spread of the variants, such as restrictions and bans on travel or transportation, stay-at-home directives, limitations on the size of gatherings, closures of work facilities, schools, public buildings and businesses, cancellation of events, including sporting events, concerts, conferences and meetings, and quarantines and lock-downs may be put into place in the future.

components.reason: Enumerates numerous potential future restrictions that would suppress operations.
Forward-looking uncertainty increases risk horizon.
Mentions some easing of restrictions, a mild mitigating note.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Lists many plausible future constraints but notes some easing; net effect is moderate risk.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic and new variants continue to impact our business, results of operations, and financial results, including the duration and magnitude of such effects, will depend on numerous evolving factors that we may not be able to accurately predict or assess.

components.reason: Acknowledges uncertainty over duration and magnitude of impacts.
Admits limited ability to predict or assess, heightening risk perception.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights unpredictability and multiple evolving variables, giving a moderate risk score.

evidence_list.snippet: In Macau, while all of our properties were open during 2021, several travel and entry restrictions were in place in Macau, Hong Kong and mainland China ... which significantly impacted visitation to MGM Macau and MGM Cotai.

components.reason: Details geographic-specific travel restrictions, showing operational constraints.
Notes significant impact on visitation, a key revenue driver.
Properties currently open—small mitigating factor.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Describes real visitation hit but mitigated slightly by being open; yields a solid mid-high score.

evidence_list.snippet: If we are unable to hire and retain sufficient employees to operate our properties or procure necessary supplies, our business, results of operations and reputation could be negatively impacted.

components.reason: Connects workforce and supply procurement risks to negative operational and reputational outcomes.
Conditional language (“if we are unable”) signals potential, not yet realized.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows potential severity in staffing and supply shortages but is still prospective; moderate score.

evidence_list.snippet: We may also face unforeseen liability or be subject to additional obligations as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, including as a result of claims alleging exposure to COVID-19 in connection with our operations or facilities or to the extent we are subject to a governmental enforcement action as a result of health and safety compliance.

components.reason: Introduces legal and compliance liabilities tied directly to pandemic.
References unforeseen or additional obligations, heightening uncertainty.
Potential regulatory enforcement noted, increasing severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Potential legal/regulatory liabilities add a significant but unquantified layer of risk.

evidence_list.snippet: At this time, we cannot predict whether jurisdictions, states or the federal government will adopt similar or more restrictive measures in the future than in the past, including stay-at-home orders or the temporary closure of all or a portion of our properties as a result of the pandemic.

components.reason: Highlights inability to forecast future shutdowns, injecting uncertainty.
Specifically contemplates full or partial property closures—high-impact scenario.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Uncertain prospect of renewed closures represents considerable potential downside, warranting a mid-high score.
